summary: Unmistakably the same idea - white lightning bolts with a coloured core striking at random positions on a black strip - but the port fires 1.6x less often, holds each bolt 1.6x less long, leaves 5x longer dark gaps, draws bolts ~30% shorter, and its LightningLength dial tops out at a third of the original's reach.
observations: Rig is a 60 px strip; neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both), no compile or runtime errors on either side, and both are stable in a late window (--skip 120 --seconds 20: orig mean 26, port mean 5, neither decaying).

Both sides draw the same primitive: a symmetric linear brightness ramp centred on a random strip position, rising from black to a white plateau and back, with a coloured (blue/cyan) core in the middle; the bolt's span is fixed for the life of one flash (no travel or growth) and it fades in and out over its lifetime. Waterfalls on both sides are horizontal streaks at random x on black.

EVENT RATE / DUTY (untouched defaults, 30 s at 20 fps, confirmed on seeds 1, 7 and 42 and at 10/20/40/60/100 fps): orig 50 flashes per 30 s, mean flash duration 0.47 s, mean dark gap 0.13 s (max 0.20 s), 22% of frames fully black. Port 31 flashes per 30 s, mean duration 0.29 s, mean dark gap 0.70 s (max 1.25 s), 70% of frames fully black. Whole-window mean brightness: orig 25, port 5.
BOLT LENGTH (--dump on peak frames, default rig, untouched dials): orig lights exactly 23 of 60 px every flash; port lights exactly 16 of 60 px. Both are consistent flash to flash.

BOLT LENGTH vs the LightningLength dial (--dump at peak frames, both sides set to the same value): orig 1 px at 0, 29 px at 0.5, 59 px at 1 - i.e. the dial spans nothing-to-whole-strip. Port 2 px at 0, 11 px at 0.5, 20 px at 1 - the dial's full-scale bolt is only a third of the strip. At LightningLength=1 the original's bolt engulfs the entire 60 px strip on every strike while the port still draws a short 20 px streak at a random position; whole-window mean brightness there is orig 64 vs port 6.

COLOURED CORE: at default dials the original shows a coloured core in 10 of 12 sampled peak frames, 1-9 px wide, and its hue varies strike to strike across a wide blue-to-cyan range (RGB 51,74,255 / 51,107,255 / 51,151,255 / 51,215,255, plus one violet 60,51,255). The port shows a core in only 3 of 12 sampled peak frames, 2-3 px wide, and its hue barely moves (38,67,255 / 38,80,255, plus one violet 80,38,255) - it reads as fixed deep blue where the original visibly cycles blue->cyan. At LightningLength=1 the gap widens: orig core 0-21 px, port core 0-3 px.

PEAK AMPLITUDE: at 20 and 40 fps every one of 50 original flashes peaks at a full 255 white plateau (mean-brightness peak tightly 59-66), while the port's mean-brightness peaks scatter 7-43. Much of that scatter is the port's sharper transient being undersampled - at 100 fps the port's peaks cluster tightly at ~42 with a discrete half-amplitude second mode at ~21, and after correcting for the shorter bolt (23/16 px) the port's per-pixel peak amplitude is comparable to the original's. Treat per-pixel amplitude as roughly right; the mean-brightness deficit is bolt length x duty cycle, not gain.

CONTROL NAME MISMATCH: the original exposes sliderLightningLength, sliderSpeed and slideroffDurationRandom (label 'offDurationRandom'); the port exposes sliderLightningLength, sliderSpeed and sliderOffDurationRandomness (label 'OffDurationRandomness'). Same count and same kinds (all sliders), but the third control's name and label differ, so a saved value would not carry across.

Both sides are frame-rate invariant in their event statistics: flash rate holds at 50/30 s (orig) and 31/30 s (port) across 10, 20, 40, 60 and 100 fps, so neither is frame-stepped. Minor caveat: at 100 fps the original's bolts stop reaching 255 (peak luminance 139-182) and lose their coloured core entirely, while the port still saturates - a small frame-rate sensitivity the original has and the port does not.

The untouched pattern has only ONE regime (continuous random strikes) over a 60 s / 5 fps survey containing 83 original events and 51 port events; the only additional regime found is the near-static one the Speed dial opens up at 0.

dials.name: sliderLightningLength
dials.origEffect: Linearly sets bolt width from 1 px at 0 to 29 px at 0.5 to 59 px at 1 - at full scale a single strike lights the whole 60 px strip. Whole-window mean brightness 2 / 32 / 64.
dials.portEffect: Same direction and roughly linear, but a third of the range: 2 px at 0, 11 px at 0.5, 20 px at 1. Whole-window mean brightness 1 / 3 / 6.

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: Inversely sets flash duration. At 0 the pattern nearly stops: 2 strikes in 30 s, each held ~14 s as a slow swelling glow, only 7% black frames. At 0.5: 57 strikes, 0.35 s each, gap 0.17 s. At 1: 55 strikes, 0.28 s each, gap 0.26 s, 49% black.
dials.portEffect: Same direction but the slow end is missing. At 0 it still fires 19 short strikes in 30 s at 1.27 s each (~11x too fast) rather than one long swell. At 0.5: 31 strikes, 0.29 s, gap 0.70 s. At 1: 24 strikes, 0.18 s, gap 1.08 s, 86% black.

dials.name: slideroffDurationRandom / sliderOffDurationRandomness
dials.origEffect: Lengthens and randomises the dark gap between strikes: mean gap 0.11 s (sd 0.03) at 0, 0.34 s (sd 0.16) at 0.5, 0.63 s (sd 0.26) at 1; black-frame fraction 18% / 41% / 55%. Flash duration is unaffected (0.48-0.50 s throughout).
dials.portEffect: Same direction, agrees at 0 (mean gap 0.12 s, sd 0.04) but over-responds badly above that: 0.77 s (sd 0.40) at 0.5 and 1.74 s (sd 0.48) at 1, roughly 2.7x the original's top-end gap; black-frame fraction 30% / 71% / 86%. Flash duration unaffected (0.28-0.31 s), as on the original. Note the control name differs from the original's.

feedback: Bolt length is the biggest visible miss. On the default rig the original lights 23 of 60 px per strike and the port 16 - but more importantly the LightningLength dial's full scale is wrong: at LightningLength=1 the original's bolt spans the entire strip (59 of 60 px) while the port's spans only 20 px. Rescale the length mapping so 0 -> ~1 px and 1 -> the whole strip, and adjust the untouched default so it lands near 23/60 px rather than 16/60 px.

The port is dark far too much of the time. At default dials the original is black 22% of frames with gaps of only 0.13 s between strikes (max 0.20 s over 30 s) - it reads as near-continuous storm flicker. The port is black 70% of frames with 0.70 s mean gaps and gaps up to 1.25 s, so it reads as occasional isolated strikes. Shorten the default off-duration by roughly 5x.

Each strike is too short-lived: original mean 0.47 s (range 0.20-0.80 s), port mean 0.29 s (range 0.10-0.45 s). Stretch the flash lifetime by ~1.6x so 50 rather than 31 strikes occupy the same 30 s at the same rate. (Rate follows once duration and gap are fixed: orig 50 per 30 s vs port 31.)

The offDurationRandom dial's gain is ~2.7x too strong above 0. The two sides agree exactly at 0 (mean gap 0.11 vs 0.12 s), but at 1 the original's mean gap is 0.63 s and the port's is 1.74 s. Scale the randomness term so full-scale lands near 0.63 s mean gap with ~0.26 s spread.

The Speed dial's slow end is missing entirely. At Speed=0 the original produces one slowly swelling bolt held for ~14 s (only 2 strikes in 30 s, 7% black frames); the port still fires 19 strikes of ~1.3 s. Extend the duration mapping so Speed=0 yields ~14 s flashes, roughly 11x the port's current slowest.

The coloured core is too small and its hue too static. On the original the core is a substantial fraction of the bolt (up to 9 of 23 px at default dials, up to 21 of 59 px at LightningLength=1) and its hue varies strike to strike right across blue-to-cyan (green channel sweeping 74-215 at R=51, B=255). The port's core is 2-3 px regardless of bolt length and sits at a near-fixed deep blue (green channel 67-80 at R=38, B=255). Widen the core in proportion to bolt length and widen the per-strike hue randomisation to reach cyan.

Rename the third control to match the original: the original's is sliderOffDurationRandom (exported name slideroffDurationRandom, label 'offDurationRandom'), the port's is sliderOffDurationRandomness. Same kind and position, but the differing name means saved values would not restore.

Per-pixel peak amplitude is already close - do not chase it. The port's white plateau reaches 255 and its per-pixel peak matches the original once bolt length is accounted for; the 5x whole-strip mean-brightness gap (25 vs 5) is entirely bolt length x duty cycle and should close on its own once the four timing/length fixes above land.

Minor: at very high frame rates (100 fps) the original stops reaching full white and drops its coloured core while the port keeps saturating. Low priority, and arguably the port behaves better, but it is a behavioural difference if exact fidelity is wanted.
